policy_use_of_the_distribution.quality_score: Q(s, approve) - Q(s, reject), with Q(s, a) = sum_i z_i p_i(s, a) = E[Z(s, a)]
policy_use_of_the_distribution.consensus: the signed sum of the stakeholders' quality scores, so the consensus is a function of the means alone
policy_use_of_the_distribution.risk_sensitivity: none - no quantile, variance or tail of Z enters a decision anywhere in this package
policy_use_of_the_distribution.where_the_distribution_acts: the learning rule only - the loss is the KL divergence against the projected n-step target distribution, so the shape of Z shapes the gradients and therefore the mean that is learnt
policy_use_of_the_distribution.consequence: Z is an internal model, not a decision variable; the statistics below measure whether that internal model is any good.

notes: greedy on the mean parameters (epsilon = 0, NoisyNet noise zeroed)
no gradient step and no replay push during the rollout

targets.n_step_reward_sum: bootstrap-free n-step reward sum at the agent's own n and gamma, truncated at the end of the run
targets.n_step_target: the agent's own training target: the n-step reward sum plus gamma^n times the double-Q bootstrap from its target network
targets.tail_return: bootstrap-free discounted tail of the appraisal stream, truncated at the end of the run

policy.statement: Of 3 stakeholder(s), 3 approved either every candidate or none of them, and 0 gave every candidate the same quality score to within 0.001 of its own magnitude.  The quality-score standard deviation runs from 0.006152 to 0.01201 across stakeholders: no stakeholder both varied that score and split its verdicts, so the policy separates no candidate from another and its approval rate is a property of the network rather than of the states it appraised.

verdict.calibration_caveat: The KS p-value is reported as a descriptive threshold, not as a significance test: an evaluation rollout's appraisals are not independent (50 share a state within an iteration, and consecutive iterations share a landscape), so the effective sample size is far below the nominal one and a p-value computed as if the sample were i.i.d. is anti-conservative at these sizes.  Read the KS statistic, which is an effect size, rather than the p-value beside it.
verdict.statement: CRPS skill against climatology is -4.582: the return distribution carries no more information than the run's marginal histogram, i.e. no state-conditional internal model is evident. The randomised PIT departs from uniformity (KS = 0.735, p = 0), so the distribution is not calibrated. Mass on the two extreme atoms averages 0.0003, so the support holds the distribution. The atom spacing is delta_z = 8 against a realised return of standard deviation 17.1 (2.14 atoms), and the run's returns occupy 24 of 51 atoms, so the support can express the variation being predicted. The mean absolute error of E[Z], the quantity that actually drives decisions, is 78.5295 against a realised return with standard deviation 17.1119. 30000 appraisals were scored over 200 iterations and take 10000 distinct realised values, so the nominal count overstates the independent information behind every statistic above.
